disclaimer: The packet counts reruns only. Necessary and sufficient are relative to the final selection, which is a local minimum; there is no causal proof and the interpretation requires human review.

hypotheses.text: The failure may require the combined effect of robot joint offsets shifting the end-effector and the basket/orange_juice_1/milk_1 position shifts altering grasp and place targets. Test: rerun with robot joints at 93.75% and basket_1 at 93.75% only (milk_1 and orange_juice_1 at reference) to see if this pair is sufficient.

Orange_juice_1 at 100% may be a critical enabler; its position shift (0.82 cm) could align with the robot's shifted grasp. Test: rerun the final selection (c37) but with orange_juice_1 at 87.5% (next untested fraction below 100%) to check if failure persists at a smaller shift.

Milk_1 at 87.5% is in the final set but its individual role is unclear. Test: rerun with milk_1 at 87.5% and robot joints at 93.75% only (basket_1 and orange_juice_1 at reference) to probe pairwise interaction.

limitations: Result is a local minimum from a limited number of reruns (budget_exhausted), one task (libero_10 task 0), and one start pair (failing 14 vs reference 4).
Necessary and sufficient are relative to the final selection (c37); removing an entity means from that set, not from the full difference.
No causal proof; the reduction is greedy and stopped early. Human review required to validate physical plausibility.

observations.text: The hypothesis ranked robot joints as the top cause, but measured shows robot joints alone (c2) and with milk_1 and orange_juice_1 (c16) do not reproduce failure. The hypothesis correctly identified robot as necessary (removing it from the final set stops failure), but wrongly predicted it would be sufficient alone.

The hypothesis ranked alphabet_soup_1 second, but it is not in the final minimal selection and was never tested in combination with the surviving entities. Measured shows alphabet_soup_1 alone (c3) does not reproduce failure, and it was dropped during reduction.

The final minimal selection (c37) requires all four components together: basket_1 at 93.75%, milk_1 at 87.5%, orange_juice_1 at 100%, and robot joints at 93.75%. No subset of these reproduces failure (c2, c3, c4, c10, c16 all pass).

Orange_juice_1 was kept at full difference (100%) without shrink testing (per minimal.shrink). Its necessity is inferred from the final set (c37) but not directly tested in isolation or smaller fractions.

evidence.meaning: The failing start itself: S F F F F (4 of 5 attempts failed), so this scene DOES reproduce the failure.
The passing reference start itself: S S S S S (0 of 5 attempts failed), so this scene passes as a reference should.

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (robot joints 100%); every other entity at the reference: S S S (0 of 3 attempts failed), so this scene does NOT reproduce the failure (the task mostly succeeded).

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (alphabet_soup_1 position 100%); every other entity at the reference: S S (0 of 2 attempts failed), so this scene does NOT reproduce the failure (the task mostly succeeded).

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (basket_1 position 100%); every other entity at the reference: S S S (0 of 3 attempts failed), so this scene does NOT reproduce the failure (the task mostly succeeded).

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (basket_1 position 100%, milk_1 position 100%, orange_juice_1 position 100%); every other entity at the reference: S S S (0 of 3 attempts failed), so this scene does NOT reproduce the failure (the task mostly succeeded).

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (milk_1 position 100%, orange_juice_1 position 100%, robot joints 100%); every other entity at the reference: S S (0 of 2 attempts failed), so this scene does NOT reproduce the failure (the task mostly succeeded).

The passing reference start with only these differences applied (basket_1 position 93.8%, milk_1 position 87.5%, orange_juice_1 position 100%, robot joints 93.8%); every other entity at the reference: F F F F (4 of 4 attempts failed), so this scene DOES reproduce the failure.

hypothesis.text: The robot's joint offsets (up to 2.2 deg) likely shift the end-effector several centimeters, misaligning grasps for both target objects. The alphabet soup moved 1.73 cm and tomato sauce 1.05 cm, so the combined pose error may push them outside the grasp tolerance. The basket moved 2.23 cm, which could also cause placement failures. I predict the simulator will show that reverting the robot joints to the reference values restores success even with the object shifts.

minimal.sentence: Moving basket_1 by 2.1 cm (of the original 2.2 cm), moving milk_1 by 2.2 cm (of the original 2.6 cm), moving orange_juice_1 by 0.8 cm (of the original 0.8 cm) and moving 5 joints of robot 94% of the way to their failing values are enough to make the policy fail from the passing start 4 (at least 4 of 5 attempts); sizes not fully shrunk; the reduction stopped early, so this is the smallest cause found so far.
shrink: basket_1 position: sizes already tested: 25%, 50%, 62.5%, 75%, 87.5% did not reproduce the failure; 81.25%, 93.75% reproduced it; 93.75% is the size kept.
milk_1 position: sizes already tested: 25%, 50%, 62.5%, 75% did not reproduce the failure; 87.5% reproduced it; 87.5% is the size kept.
robot joints: sizes already tested: 25%, 50%, 62.5%, 75%, 81.25%, 87.5% did not reproduce the failure; 93.75% reproduced it; 93.75% is the size kept.
orange_juice_1: kept at its full difference; its size was not shrunk before the reduction stopped (untested).
